Swift Concurrency

Health Check

The app uses Swift Concurrency deliberately: Features own shared state, screens own their interactions, and provider requests can run independently.

✓
Assessment
Strong concurrency design
Clear ownership, independent provider refreshes and explicitly coordinated reminder updates.

What is working well

✓

Startup starts Features directly

The app delegate signals AppModel synchronously; Features start their own work.

Evidence: RocketLaunchApp.swift:22–29; AppModel.swift:17–25.

✓

Shared refreshes have an owner

The schedule Feature joins provider requests, tracks waiters and resumes callers without waiting for the optional cache write.

Evidence: LaunchScheduleFeature.swift:166–292.

✓

Screen selections stay independent

Navigation selections belong to each screen and detail screens receive selected launch values.

Evidence: UpcomingViewModel.swift:4–15; LaunchDetailView.swift:3–13.

✓

Reminder changes have an explicit persistence policy

The Feature sequences reminder writes and coordinates notification effects with confirmed state.

Evidence: LaunchScheduleFeature.swift:571–640, 716–752, 805–870.

✓

Storage and network work have separate owners

Provider and persistence actors perform their respective operations; the schedule Feature owns application state.

Evidence: NetworkingManager.swift:4–10; LaunchScheduleCache.swift:16–61.

How the app’s work flows

Start the app

Path: App delegate → AppModel.applicationDidFinishLaunching → schedule and settings Features start loading.

Task ownership: The delegate calls synchronously; the Features retain their own loading tasks.

Isolation: MainActor delegate and AppModel; Features coordinate work with actors.

Loading is signalled directly without delaying the callback for downloads.

Refresh the schedule from the Changes screen

Path: Changes screen → UpdatesViewModel → LaunchRefreshTasks → LaunchScheduleFeature → provider repository; cache saves independently.

Task ownership: Screen retains a task; the Feature tracks shared provider work and each waiter.

Isolation: MainActor presentation and Feature; provider and network actors perform their own work.

Repeated callers join provider work, obsolete request IDs are rejected, and cache persistence does not hold up refresh completion.

Change the colour theme

Path: Settings picker → SettingsViewModel → SettingsFeature → ThemePersistence.

Task ownership: SettingsFeature retains and sequences theme-write tasks.

Isolation: MainActor Feature delegates storage to ThemePersistence actor.

Writes wait for earlier writes and publish the selected theme after persistence succeeds.

Monitor the schedule while a scene is active

Path: Scene phase task → AppModel → shared schedule monitor.

Task ownership: SwiftUI owns each scene task; the Feature owns one shared monitor.

Isolation: MainActor coordination; timer suspends between updates.

Scenes join one monitor. The last departing caller cancels it, without cancelling downloads.

Open or retry the privacy policy

Path: Privacy View → PrivacyPolicyViewModel → SettingsFeature → bundled policy loader.

Task ownership: SwiftUI owns the initial task; the ViewModel retains retry work; the Feature shares the file read.

Isolation: MainActor presentation; bundled file loader actor.

Repeated reads share work, while cancellation and request identity guard screen publication.

Create, update, load and remove reminders

Path: Detail or Reminders screen → screen ViewModel → schedule Feature → reminder persistence and notification actors.

Task ownership: Screen ViewModels retain intents; the Feature retains and sequences persistence and notification work.

Isolation: MainActor Feature and presentation; persistence and notification clients use actors.

The Feature persists proposed reminder state before publishing it and tracks notification installation and cleanup.

Retry loading saved settings

Path: Settings screen → SettingsViewModel → SettingsFeature → theme persistence actor.

Task ownership: The ViewModel owns the retry task and the Feature joins its shared load.

Isolation: MainActor screen and Feature; persistence actor performs file work.

Repeated retry taps join the screen task and the Feature shares its current load.

Navigate, filter and select launch details

Path: A screen changes its own selection or filter → a destination receives the selected value.

Task ownership: Navigation and filtering are synchronous UI actions.

Isolation: SwiftUI and MainActor ViewModels read Feature snapshots.

Independent screens retain their own selections; detail screens receive the selected launch snapshot.

✓

  • ✓Consistent concurrency structure.
  • ✓The schedule Feature coordinates shared requests, storage and reminders.
  • ✓Screen selections and presentation remain local.
  • ✓Shared refreshes have a clear cancellation policy.
